artifacts.summary: Closed both halves of the snapshot-artifact containment defect: git-snapshot.sh's --no-revert enumeration is now file_scope-narrowed, and git-commit-phase.sh's fixed stage_paths seed conditionally excludes both snapshot artifact classes; registered untracked-backup-*/ as the 28th ephemeral runtime-file class member; two regression cases demonstrated RED before the fix and green after, deployed clean.

completion_data.completion_summary: Fixed both cooperating defects that let git-snapshot.sh's --no-revert artifacts contaminate phase commits with other tasks' files: narrowed the untracked-file backup to the dispatching task's file_scope, added conditional exclusion entries to git-commit-phase.sh's fixed staging seed, and registered the backup directory as the 28th ephemeral runtime-file class member. Two regression cases were demonstrated failing against the unmodified scripts before the fix landed and pass after; deploy-headless.sh reported RESULT=landed_verify_clean.

memory_candidates.content: scripts/lib/runtime-file-patterns.sh's runtime_file_dir_basename_for_hit() originally assumed every directory-class ephemeral-runtime-file member has a FIXED basename (e.g. '.lock', '.dispatch'). A member whose directory NAME itself varies per invocation (e.g. a timestamp suffix) needs its RUNTIME_FILE_DIR_BASENAME entry to be a glob pattern instead, and the lookup function generalized to: detect a glob-metacharacter basename, then walk the hit's own path segments (split on '/') testing each against the glob, returning the REAL matched segment (never the pattern) since callers build a 'git rm -r --cached <dir>' path from the return value. This generalization is provably backward-compatible when no pre-existing basename contains a glob metacharacter.

test-runtime-file-tracking.sh (and the deploy-tree-first/source-store-fallback idiom it shares with check-runtime-file-tracking.sh and init-specs.sh) deliberately prefers the DEPLOYED tree (.claude/) when all three of {check script, lib, standards doc} are present there together, falling back to the source store only otherwise -- documented purpose: never pair a stale deployed doc against a freshly-edited source-store lib. Consequence: running this specific suite against a source-store edit BEFORE a deploy silently validates the stale deployed state, not the edit, with no error. init-specs.sh and check-runtime-file-tracking.sh themselves have NO deploy-root-guard and resolve paths relative to their own SCRIPT_DIR, so invoking the source-store copy of EITHER directly does exercise the fresh edit; generate-context-line-counts.sh needs an explicit REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) env var to bypass its own deploy-root-guard the same way.

When git-commit-phase.sh's Phase-Commit Containment Self-Check drops a files_touched path not in the task's declared file_scope, it deposits the path into .return-meta.json's proposed_file_scope and the commit otherwise succeeds (rc=0) minus that path. The correct remedy is ONE scoped follow-up commit of exactly that path via git-commit-scoped.sh directly -- never a second git-commit-phase.sh call for the same path, since that would re-run the identical, still-unwidened Containment Self-Check and drop it again (the wrapper's own file_scope is read fresh from state.json each call, never unioned with proposed_file_scope).

sapience_notes.subject: test-runtime-file-tracking.sh's tree-resolution order
sapience_notes.value: It deliberately prefers the deployed .claude/ tree over the agent-system source store when both have the check script, lib, and standards doc present together -- a pre-deploy run of this specific suite silently validates stale deployed state rather than fresh source-store edits, with no error signal distinguishing the two cases.

sapience_notes.subject: init-specs.sh and check-runtime-file-tracking.sh deploy-root-guard exemption
sapience_notes.value: Neither script sources deploy-root-guard.sh; both resolve paths relative to their own SCRIPT_DIR, so invoking the source-store copy directly (bash agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/<name>.sh) exercises a freshly-edited source-store lib without first redeploying -- unlike generate-context-line-counts.sh, which needs an explicit REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) env var to bypass its own guard the same way.

sapience_notes.subject: __WHOLE_TREE__ file_scope sentinel scope
sapience_notes.value: This sentinel is specifically a mechanism for declaring a claim over the whole DEPLOYED tree (.claude/**); it is not a blanket wildcard admitting arbitrary source-store paths outside the task's own explicitly-declared file_scope list. A source-store test file not individually named in file_scope was still dropped by git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check even with __WHOLE_TREE__ present.

sapience_notes.subject: runtime_file_dir_basename_for_hit() generalization constraint
sapience_notes.value: A directory-class ephemeral-runtime-file member whose directory NAME itself varies per invocation (not just its contents) requires the shared library's basename-matching accessor to support a glob-style basename, resolved against the hit's real path segments at lookup time rather than treated as a literal -- the pre-existing 27 members all used fixed literals, so this generalization was previously unneeded.

sapience_notes.subject: git-snapshot.sh --no-revert mode untracked-backup narrowing
sapience_notes.value: The untracked-file backup this mode writes is now filtered through the dispatching task's declared file_scope (own directory always admitted), with a named stderr warning and own-directory-only fallback when file_scope cannot be resolved, deliberately weaker than the reverting modes' fail-closed refusal because --no-revert destroys nothing and must stay available on a RED tree.

sapience_notes.subject: git-commit-phase.sh fixed-scope snapshot-artifact exclusion
sapience_notes.value: The fixed stage_paths seed now conditionally subtracts working-progress-*.patch and untracked-backup-* via an explicit :(exclude) pathspec entry, injected only when git check-ignore -q does not already report the concrete on-disk hit as covered -- naming an already-ignored path in an explicit exclude entry would make git add abort the whole add.

sapience_notes.subject: untracked-backup-*/ vs working-progress-*.patch ephemeral-class disposition
sapience_notes.value: The backup directory joined the canonical ephemeral runtime-file class (28th member) because it is a literal duplicate of content that is itself untracked and never deleted by the --no-revert mode that writes it; the patch file deliberately did not join, since it is the sole durable record of a --no-revert snapshot's tracked-change diff and remains tracked-eligible under the task directory by that script's own documented design.
